items.summary: If Wednesday is the last we see of Kaiden Guhle for an extended period, this skid the Canadiens are on could become a major slide.
items.body: DENVER — The Montreal Canadiens might have a major problem on their blue line, and there’s no telling how quickly they’ll be able to solve it. It was already a problem before the Canadiens lost 6-0 to the Colorado Avalanche Wednesday — their most lopsided loss of the season and one that cemented their first three-game losing streak (with all three losses coming in regulation) in just over a year — but it became a much bigger problem when Kaiden Guhle left in the 10 th minute of the second period. The 25-year-old took a heavy hit from behind from Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog and was slow to get back to his feet. The last we saw of him was in a scrum with Landeskog at the end of that shift, leaving the Canadiens down a man and down 2-0. If that’s the last we see of Guhle for any extended period, this skid his team is on could become a major slide. “It’s a tough loss,” said Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki , “a tough guy to replace.” Guhle has been Montreal’s most stable defenceman this year, a punishing presence in his own zone, the go-to option for tough match ups and a minute-muncher in crunch time. He’s been exactly what the Canadiens have needed him to be in Mike Matheson ’s absence. That’s where this problem started, with Matheson going down on Nov. 12. We’re talking about Montreal’s most-used defenceman over the last three seasons and change, their best skater on the back end, and the guy who’d have almost certainly played alongside Guhle Wednesday had he not been missing his 17 th game of the season. items.title: Canadiens’ Florian Xhekaj receives match penalty for slew foot
items.body: It was a chippy affair between the Montreal Canadiens and Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday night, and Florian Xhekaj was right in the middle of all of it. It culminated late in the third period, when the forward was handed a match penalty for slew-footing Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov, subsequently ending his night. The infraction happened with just over a minute remaining in the game as the Canadiens were down 6-0. The whistle had just sounded when Xhekaj tripped up Svechkov and was assessed an intent-to-injure penalty. That would be five of Xhekaj's 22 penalty minutes on the evening, as he was also assessed a 10-minute misconduct in the second period. A match penalty comes with an automatic ejection and review from the league. Florian wouldn't be the only Xhekaj to amass a fair few PIMs on Wednesday, as brother Arber — a Canadiens defenceman — wracked up 16 of his own. The brothers combined for 33 of the 42 total penalty minutes in this game. Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog wasn't thrilled with the antics of the Xhekaj brothers, telling reporters that they "have to use (their) head a little bit." "The Xhekaj brothers, they wanted to get involved so we'll see what's going to happen with that," Landeskog told reporters after the game . "I think for one of the most storied franchises and one of the most respected franchises in all of hockey, and you've got two guys doing that." Florian, who has played 17 career NHL games, has 54 penalty minutes. There will be no chance for revenge, though, on either side as Wednesday's match wrapped up the season series between the two inter-conference teams.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The NHL Department of Player Safety announced New Jersey Devils defenseman Brendan Dillon will have a hearing Thursday for an illegal check to the head on Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk during their game Wednesday night. Dillon, 36, delivered the hit midway through the first period after Mateychuk crossed the Devils’ blue line and made a pass to Jack Williams. The New Jersey defender made the hit, then Mateychuk struggled to get back up while a scrum ensued. Dillon received a five-minute major and a game misconduct. He finished the night with 15 penalty minutes and 3:23 of ice time. Meanwhile, Mateychuk left the game and did not return. He had one shot in 3:51. Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness, who coached Dillon during his time with the Winnipeg Jets , told reporters after the game he didn’t think he was a dirty player. “He’s a hard player, and he caught him in a bad spot,” Bowness said . “That’s a bad hit.” Dillion has a goal and assist with 37 penalty minutes in 16 games with the Devils in 2026-27. Through 16 NHL seasons, the New Westminister, B.C., native has 43 goals and 186 assists for 229 points and 1,051 penalty minutes in 1,072 career regular-season games. As for Mateychuk, the 22-year old has four goals and three assists for seven points in 22 games this season. In 142 regular-season games, he has 21 goals and 30 assists for 51 points.

items.title: Devils’ Dillon to have hearing for check to head of Blue Jackets’ Mateychuk
items.body: Brenden Dillon is set to receive a call from the NHL's Department of Player Safety. The Department announced that Dillon will have a hearing on Thursday for an illegal check to the head and interference against Columbus Blue Jackets defenceman Denton Mateychuk in their game Wednesday. Dillon received a match penalty for the hit, which came in the first period as Mateychuk skated into the New Jersey zone after delivering a pass along the blue line. The Devils defenceman appeared to leave his feet to deliver the hit on Mateychuk, who had kept his eyes on the puck to his right. Mateychuk stayed on the Columbus bench through the second period, but didn't play in the frame and didn't come back out for the third. He entered concussion protocol after the game. Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness told reporters post-game that Mateychuk "feels fine" Dillon also received a five-minute major on the play. He had logged just 3:23 of ice time before the ejection in what ended as a 3-2 New Jersey shootout win. The 36-year-old was suspended for an illegal check to the head of Pittsburgh Penguins forward Noel Acciari in 2024.

items.summary: Devon Toews scored twice in a 1:33 span during the second period, Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 27 shots and the refreshed Colorado Avalanche beat the Montreal Canadiens 6-0 on Wednesday night.
items.body: DENVER — Devon Toews scored twice in a 1:33 span during the second period, Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 27 shots and the refreshed Colorado Avalanche beat the Montreal Canadiens 6-0 on Wednesday night. Artturi Lehkonen, Logan O’Connor, Martin Necas and Gabriel Landeskog also had goals for the Avalanche, who were back in action for the first time since a 4-0 win over Anaheim last Thursday. Colorado looked energized by the break, especially in the second period with a three-goal spurt. Colorado posted its third consecutive home shutout, with Blackwood responsible for two and Scott Wedgewood one. It's the second time in Avalanche history they have notched three straight home shutouts, according to NHL research. They also accomplished the feat in November 2001 behind Hall of Fame goaltender Patrick Roy. The Canadiens dropped to 0-2 since acquiring Dylan Larkin in a deal with Detroit. Jacob Fowler stopped 32 shots. Cale Makar had three assists in his return after missing three games with a lower-body injury. Colorado outscored Montreal 10-1 in the two meetings this season. The game turned chippy in the third. Florian Xhekaj drew a major near the end of the contest. Defenseman Brent Burns took a hit in the back from Arber Xhekaj late in the third period and momentarily stayed down on the ice before heading to the bench. Burns has played in 1,031 straight games. He's 33 away from tying the NHL’s streak for consecutive games held by Phil Kessel (1,064). Parker Kelly appeared to catch the blade of Arber Xhekaj's skate near his wrist after a hit in the corner during the second period. Kelly went to the locker room moments after the play but returned to the bench.

items.body: Forwards combine for four points in win against Senators after being out since early October SUNRISE, Fla. -- The Florida Panthers had the band back together for the first time in a long time Wednesday. Captain Aleksander Barkov and forward Brad Marchand returned to the lineup after each had played just two games this season due to injuries early in October. Both were instrumental in Florida’s 5-3 win against the Ottawa Senators at Amerant Bank Arena. Marchand, who had been out since injuring his left knee in a 2-1 win against the Los Angeles Kings on Oct. 6, assisted on three of the Panthers’ first four goals. “It was great to be out there, but even better seeing ‘Barky’ back again,” Marchand said. Barkov missed the entire 2025-26 season with a right knee injury only to injury his left knee in a 4-3 overtime loss to the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 1, the Panthers’ second game of the season. He scored into an empty net for his team’s final goal Wednesday, helping the Panthers end the first-place Senators’ nine-game point streak (7-0-2) and pull within one point of second in the ultra-competitive Atlantic Division. “I feel like I got better once the game started going,” Barkov said. “The second, third period were better. Obviously it takes time to get used to playing against a really good team. There’s not much space on the ice. You have to kind of figure it out. But playing with good players and a good time made it easier for me to find my rhythm.” The game Wednesday was the first time the Panthers got to see the team they envisioned in the offseason when landed forward Brady Tkachuk in a trade with Ottawa and added goalie Jacob Markstrom in a trade with the New Jersey Devils, among other moves. items.body: Film tells tale of development, impact of ‘The Great One’s’ Easton aluminum model Wayne Gretzky didn’t so much grip a hockey stick as he twirled a magic wand, doing things with a puck that had never been imagined, much less witnessed for real. Like any skilled magician, ‘The Great One’s’ act deceived the eye. It made observers do a double- or triple-take, trying to process Gretzky’s sleight of hand that had just made the seemingly impossible very possible indeed. The greatest point-scorer in NHL history routinely shredded the opposition with highlight-reel goals and his setup of teammates. Gretzky’s 1,963 career assists alone puts him atop the League’s all-time points list, before you tack on his 894 goals. He was lethal with his heavy Titan wood stick for the Edmonton Oilers and in his first two seasons with Los Angeles upon his 1988 trade to the Kings. But then, in 1990, Gretzky shook the NHL and the entire business of hockey to its foundation, switching from his Titan lumber to a revolutionary two-piece aluminum “twig” produced by Easton Sports of Van Nuys, California. Gretzky’s Easton HXP5100 aluminum stick is the subject of a fascinating new NHL documentary, “The Stick That Changed The Game,” to be released Nov. 27 on the League’s YouTube channel. Blake Coleman had two goals and Bobby Brink also scored for the Western Conference-leading Wild (18-4-5), who were a franchise-best 12-0-3 in their previous 15 games. After Coleman cut the deficit to one with 4:04 left, Mammoth center Barret Hayton was whistled 19 seconds later for a double-minor penalty for high-sticking Joel Eriksson Ek. The Wild had a power play for the remainder of regulation but managed only two shots. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves for his first win in seven starts since Oct. 24 and Lawson Crouse and Dmitri Simashev scored for the Mammoth, whose second-period leads of 3-1 and 4-2 gave the Wild a two-goal deficit for the first time since their last regulation loss at Calgary on Oct. 22. Crouse’s tip-in of Vincent Trocheck’s shot in the first period stopped Minnesota’s scoring-first streak at 15 straight games. That was tied for the second-longest run in NHL history and best in the league since Montreal in 1972. The Canadiens have the record with 18 consecutive games, set during the 1959-60 season. Kirill Kaprizov’s franchise-record streak of 15 straight games with a point ended, as did his run of six consecutive games with multiple assists. That was the second-longest streak in NHL history, behind Wayne Gretzky's eight in 1984. Kaprizov went without a point for just the third time in 27 games, with linemates Eriksson Ek and Matt Boldy also producing at a prolific rate this season. items.title: Ducks’ Cutter Gauthier becomes first American to score 21 goals in 14 games
items.body: Only three full seasons into his NHL career, Cutter Gauthier is rewriting record books. The Anaheim Ducks star forward has been on a near-unparalleled scoring surge in recent weeks, and after yet another goal against the San Jose Sharks on Wednesday night, he hit a mark last reached by Mario Lemieux more than three decades ago. With his 21st goal in the last 14 games, Gauthier became the first player to accomplish the feat since Lemieux in the 1992-93 season, and became the only American in NHL history to do so. He hit the mark with just under five minutes left in the first period against the Sharks, finishing off a power-play marker set up by Jackson LaCombe and Mikael Granlund to give his side a 3-0 lead. The only other players to score 21 in 14 games are Lemieux (1992-93 and 1988-89), Teeme Selanne (1992-93), Alexander Mogilny (1992-93), Bernie Nichols (1988-89) and Wayne Gretzky (1980-81, 1981-82, and 1983-84). Gauthier's run started on Oct. 29, when he potted two goals against the Buffalo Sabres. He went on to score back-to-back hat tricks against the Ottawa Senators and Vancouver Canucks, then grabbed two more against the Pittsburgh Penguins and St. Louis Blues over the course of his streak. With the majority of his goals — 19 of them — coming since the calendar turned to November, he may set the record for most goals in a calendar month in the coming days, with Selanne atop the ladder with 20. Gauthier is only the eighth player and second American to score 19 in a calendar month, and has two more games against the Los Angeles Kings on Nov. 27 and 28 to break the record. On the season, the 22-year-old has 23 goals — tied for the league lead with Leon Draisaitl of the Edmonton Oilers — and nine assists in 25 games.

It’s not immediately clear where the injury happened but he exited during the second period, ending his night after just 6:34 on the ice. In a contract year the 27-year-old has stepped up in a big way, already at 13 points in 24 games when his career high is 22. Known to be a dependable shutdown winger, Holmberg has shown new elements to his game, being rewarded with time on the power play as well as a top six deployment, including tonight on Brayden Point ’s wing. Going 7-4-0 since star Nikita Kucherov ’s unexpected and league-shaking trade request , the Bolts lost to Carolina tonight and haven’t had the smoothest past few days. Last Sunday the superstar was benched in a convincing loss to Buffalo. Through it all, Holmberg has stayed in Cooper’s good graces, earning more shifts that night and continuing to cement himself as a vital middle-six role player. items.summary: Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov returned to the Florida lineup in style, with Marchand getting three assists and Barkov scoring an empty-netter to help the Panthers beat the Ottawa Senators 5-3 on Wednesday night.
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov returned to the Florida lineup in style, with Marchand getting three assists and Barkov scoring an empty-netter to help the Panthers beat the Ottawa Senators 5-3 on Wednesday night. Anton Lundell, Sam Bennett, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen also had goals for Florida, which got both Marchand and Barkov back after each missed nearly two months with knee injuries suffered in the season's opening week. It was Barkov's first home game for Florida since the final game of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final. Jacob Markstrom stopped 25 shots. Dylan Cozens and Philip Tomasino had goals 41 seconds apart early in the second period for Ottawa, with Artem Zub and Jake Sanderson picking up assists on both as the Senators took a 2-1 lead. The rest of the game was all Florida, and Ottawa's nine-game point streak (7-0-2) came to an end. Michael Amadio scored with 51 seconds left for the Senators. Mikkola tied it for Florida midway through the second period and Marchand — stickhandling around a pair of Senators — set up Lundell for the goal that gave the Panthers a 3-2 lead going into the third. Bennett's goal with 10:43 left sealed it, beating Ottawa goalie Linus Ullmark from close range for a 4-2 lead. The play started with Florida goalie Jacob Markstrom coming way out of the net, nearly to the blue line, to send a loose puck to the right-wing boards. Marchand played it to Lundell, who set up Bennett. Ullmark entered the game as the NHL's leader this season with a 1.44 goals-against average and a .938 save percentage. The Panthers solved him, becoming the first team to score four on Ullmark this season. In his first 13 appearances this season, Ullmark allowed three goals only once — in a 4-3 overtime win over Colorado on Nov. 12.

items.summary: Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night.
items.body: BOSTON — Morgan Barron scored the tie-breaking goal late in the second period, Nico Daws made 21 saves, and the Winnipeg Jets added to their surge with a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins on Wednesday night. Kyle Connor and Josh Morrissey each had a goal for Winnipeg, which won its fourth straight road game and improved to 9-1-1 in its last 11 overall. Mark Scheifele, the Jets' career goals leader, added an empty-netter for the 381st of his career. Morgan Geekie and Fraser Minten scored for the Bruins, who dropped the second of their season-high six-game homestand. Jeremy Swayman stopped 14 shots. Barron’s goal came with 2:07 left in the second when he poked the puck between Swayman’s pads to make it 3-2 after the goalie mishandled the rebound of Mario Ferraro’s shot. Boston’s Tanner Jeannot and Winnipeg’s Tyrel Bauer squared off in a lengthy fight midway into the opening period that featured numerous haymakers. Trailing in the second, Boston tied it at 2 when Minten, positioned directly in front of the net, tipped Mason Lohrei’s shot by Daws at 10:57. Morrissey’s slap shot from the slot beat Swayman and gave the Jets a 2-1 edge late in the opening period. Off since a 7-5 victory over Washington at home Saturday, the Bruins had tied it at 1 on Geekie’s power-play goal off a pretty pass across the front of the net by David Pastrnak at 6:11. Connor’s wrister from the left circle made it 1-0 just 65 seconds into the game. The Bruins won the first meeting between the teams in overtime on Oct. 2.

items.title: Farabee has goal and assist to help Flames beat Penguins
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Joel Farabee had a goal and an assist and the Calgary Flames beat the Pittsburgh Penguins 6-3 on Wednesday night. Maxim Tsyplakov and Brennan Othmann also each had a goal and an assist for the Flames, who snapped a three-game losing streak. Ryan Strome, Jonathan Castagna and Yegor Sharangovich also scored. Zayne Parekh had an assist to pass Miles Zaharko for the fifth-most points by a Flames’ defenceman younger than 21. Evgeni Malkin passed Bryan Trottier for 19th-most points in NHL history with a power-play goal and an assist for Pittsburgh. Malkin, who missed the last two games because of an injury, had his 382nd multipoint game and tied Teemu Selanne for fourth among players born and trained outside of North America. Rickard Rakell also had a power-play goal and Tommy Novak also scored. The Penguins scored two home power-play goals for the first time since an Oct. 3 win against Montreal. Arturs Silovs stopped 20 shots for the Penguins, who lost their fifth straight. Pittsburgh, last in the Eastern Conference, has lost 10 of 12 overall. The Flames won their 64th straight game when scoring four or more goals. They’re one four-goal win from tying the New York Rangers’ 65-game run from 2011-14, the longest mark in NHL history. The streak began with a 4-2 victory over Tampa Bay on Dec. 16, 2023. This season, the Flames are 7-0-0 when scoring at least four goals.

items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Recall Artur Akhtyamov By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 2:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Toronto Maple Leafs recalled netminder Artur Akhtyamov from the Toronto Marlies in the AHL. Toronto had two open roster spots, so they didn’t need to make a corresponding roster move. As of now, there is no known reason why the Maple Leafs called up Akhtyamov. Toronto has an upcoming back-to-back series in Boston and Pittsburgh, leading to speculation that the Maple Leafs might rest Sergei Bobrovsky due to his recent struggles on the ice. However, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman confirmed that Bobrovsky will start on Saturday against the Penguins. Since there aren’t any goaltending injuries to speak of, Anthony Stolarz will likely start Friday against the Bruins Still, considering they have the roster space, Toronto is likely using Akhtyamov as insurance for their upcoming back-to-back. The Maple Leafs are well aware that injuries are a constant concern. As for Akhtyamov, today’s transaction is his third call-up of the 2026-27 campaign. Unfortunately, he hasn’t appeared for Toronto yet. He’s played exclusively for the Marlies, going 3-3-3 in nine contests with an .886 SV% and 2.92 GAA. Still, it was around this time last season that Akhtyamov made his NHL debut in a loss to the Edmonton Oilers. Still, most of his season was spent with the Marlies, where he posted a 21-12-4 record with a .904 SV% and 2.88 GAA. The Maple Leafs signed him to a three-year, $2.7MM ($900K AAV) extension in March of last season.

items.summary: The Edmonton Oilers will have plenty of time to unwind over the next month. Mark Spector checks in ahead of a two-day break with some news and notes.
items.body: EDMONTON — It’s time to breathe for the Edmonton Oilers , a team about to enter a friendly stretch in the schedule after playing eight straight games in a new city every night. “I think the last two weeks have been a lot,” admitted Leon Draisaitl , the NHL’s league leader with 23 goals. “With that being said, all the teams have stretches like that. We're all going through the same thing at some point during the season.” How does a hockey team full of 20- or 30-somethings unwind after a long stretch of travel and a four-game losing streak? How else? They’ll gather to watch NFL games on Thursday, preferably at the home of any married American players whose wives may perhaps be putting a turkey on. One day off is an eternity in the NHL, a league where you have to relax fast, and a wicked schedule always moves on to some other team. “If you looked at our schedule coming up now, we’ve got four two-day blocks (between games) and the longest Christmas break in the history of the NHL (six days off). So we're set up pretty good here,” said head coach Mike Babcock. Some news and notes around the Oilers as they step away for a day and a half. Call them, Spec’s Checks: With a back-to-back home-and-home against the Kraken on Friday-Saturday, expect Edmonton to try to retrieve their defensive game Friday night at Rogers Place against a Kraken team they’ve owned for a while now. Since November 1, Washington has allowed an average of 5.11 goals per game , easily clearing the Chicago Blackhawks and Vancouver Canucks for worst in the NHL. But even as they struggle mightily to keep pucks out of their own net, they’ve had far less trouble scoring on opponents. The Capitals have averaged 3.22 goals per game, good for 15th in the league — not stellar, certainly, and likely somewhat the result of score effects, but a far cry from their metrics on the other end of the ice. Asked Wednesday whether the Caps have neglected their defense to chase offensive opportunities, head coach Spencer Carbery agreed wholeheartedly. That’s something of a new issue for Carbery’s Capitals. However, this tournament doesn't dictate what a player's whole career will look like. Who are the most noteworthy omissions from world junior rosters? The world juniors provides prospects with an excellent opportunity to announce themselves to the hockey world every year. Draft-eligible players can cement themselves as top prospects, and drafted prospects can compete against the world's best while representing their country at a major event. But throughout time, we've seen that the world juniors don't dictate what a player's career will look like. Some players have looked like superstars at the tournament and went on to have lacklustre NHL careers. Some struggled, but went on to have outstanding NHL careers. His timeline for a return from a lower-body injury was recently extended to 12 weeks. MacKinnon and Makar both left in the second period of the Avalanche’s 4-3 overtime loss in Ottawa on Nov. 12. MacKinnon went down to his knees holding his right hip after being pushed while trying to gain control of the puck. Makar left favoring his right leg. Haven’t had it for a while." The two-time Norris Trophy winner as the NHL’s top defenseman has five goals and 18 assists in 19 games this season. He's averaging more than 22 minutes on the ice and ready to take on that kind workload. “Anytime you come back from an injury, you've got to be ready to go,” Makar said. “Regardless if I’m playing 30 (minutes), if I’m playing 15, whatever team needs me for, I’ll be there for it.” Avalanche coach Jared Bednar echoed that: “He’s cleared to play,” he said. “He's going to play.” Because of a quirk in the schedule, the Avalanche haven't played since a 4-0 win over Anaheim last Thursday. “A little bit weird,” Makar said of the prolonged break. “To be out for two weeks-ish and really miss ... three games, I’ll take it.” The team went 2-1 in his absence. "Obviously, a weird scenario where I only miss a couple games over a two-week stretch mid-season, but again, just trying to stay active, get back in the groove of things myself,” Makar said. “A lot of skating, and yeah, hopefully feel good moving on here.” Colorado center Nathan MacKinnon sustained a lower-body injury in the same game. items.body: Register Login Ducks Reassign Noah Warren By Brennan McClain | at November 25, 2026 12:00 pm Yesterday afternoon, the Anaheim Ducks announced they reassigned defenseman Noah Warren to the San Diego Gulls in the AHL. The transaction drops Anaheim to 22 players on the active roster. Until yesterday, Warren had been a constant on the Ducks’ defensive corps all season. After playing two years for the Gulls, the former 42nd overall pick cracked Anaheim’s opening-night roster to begin the 2026-27 campaign. In San Diego, Warren registered two goals and 16 points in 122 games from 2024 to 2026. There’s no question the 6’5″, 216lbs defender isn’t known for his offensive skills. Still, Warren didn’t look entirely out of place with the Ducks this season, tallying six assists in 23 contests on a -3 rating while averaging 15:33 of ice time per game. Regardless of yesterday’s demotion, Warren should expect to hold down a long-term spot with the Ducks relatively soon. Anaheim lost multiple defenders this past offseason, and although he likely won’t contribute a ton offensively, Warren’s mobility, especially at his size, makes him a useful talent to have on the back end. Meanwhile, the Ducks could go multiple different directions with their newfound roster spot. Currently, Anaheim is waiting for forwards A.J. Greer and Beckett Sennecke to return from injury. Both Greer and Sennecke are projected to return toward the end of November, so the Ducks may activate one of them soon.

Hagel, 28, has been activated off the Lightning’s injured reserve list after missing the past three games with a lower-body injury. The 6’2″ winger currently ranks third on the Lightning in scoring with 24 points (13 goals, 11 assists) through 20 games this season. Girgensons, 32, sustained an upper-body injury against the Washington Capitals on Nov. 17 and missed the next two games while recovering. The 6’3″ center has one goal and four points and has gone 55.5 percent in the faceoff dot through 18 games this year. Hagel took part in the Bolts’ optional morning skate ahead of their game against the Hurricanes on Wednesday, while Girgensons did not. Lightning head coach Jon Cooper said earlier this week that the plan was for both forwards to return against Carolina. items.title: Babcock explains decision not to challenge possible Oilers goal vs. Vegas
items.summary: Head coach Mike Babcock ultimately chose not to challenge the play. The Oilers still rallied to tie the game 2-2 but unravelled in the third period to lose 5-3.
items.body: Already down 2-0 early to the Vegas Golden Knights , the Edmonton Oilers got a puck past Carter Hart in the first period on Tuesday, but the play was ruled no-goal. The reason? Officials determined Oilers forward Mathieu Joseph had interfered with Hart on the play while battling for position with Vegas defenceman Rasmus Andersson . That left the Oilers with a choice. Do they challenge the ruling and try to cut the deficit in half or let the game play on? Head coach Mike Babcock ultimately chose not to challenge the play. The Oilers still rallied to tie the game 2-2 but unravelled in the third period to lose 5-3. "Our guy went in on his own and then he bumped their stick," Babcock said after the game when asked about not challenging. "I haven't been back very long, but I've just learned they don't (overturn) anything. So unless you're 100 per cent sure, why be shorthanded?" Joseph said he didn't feel contact with Hart in the heat of the battle but conceded it was risky to challenge at that stage of the game. "It was a pretty tough call," Joseph said. "I was just trying to get in there. I feel like I'm getting pushed back a little bit ... Sometimes the bounces don't go your way, but you've got to stick with it."

When Stan Wong isn't tending to injured hockey players as a head athletic trainer, he's working at the Oriental Chow Mein Company, a Massachusetts business his family established after they immigrated from China more than a century ago. "Whether I'm a chow mein maker or an athletic trainer, I strive to be the best I can be, and I don't take that lightly," Wong said. "That's how much I push myself. That's what I expect." For more than 40 years, Wong given his best as a beloved head athletic trainer with the Washington Capitals (1986-99) and Florida Panthers (1999-2002), and for 59 United States teams in international competitions from world championships to the Winter Olympics. Wong's dedication to players, his professionalism and infectious personality are why the 68-year-old from Fall River, Massachusetts, is being inducted into the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame on Nov. 30 in Washington, D.C. "I think the players look up to Stan as a considerate and trusted person," said John Vanbiesbrouck, USA Hockey assistant executive director of hockey operations and a 2007 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame inductee. "He's a glue guy that's around all the time. And some of the former (Team USA players), they're always asking, 'Where's Stan? Is he involved?' items.title: Oilers show natural signs of fatigue in loss to Vegas after taxing road trip
items.summary: The Oilers looked tired, performed tired, and made tired mistakes in a loss to the Golden Knights on Tuesday, It’s just not easy for a team to be at its best after a six-game Eastern road swing.
items.body: EDMONTON — A hockey player will never just come out and say it. Maybe it’s because a hockey fan who goes to work for far longer hours for waaaay less pay simply doesn’t want to hear it. The Edmonton Oilers looked tired, performed tired, and made tired mistakes in their 5-3 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday, and for the first time in the Mike Babcock era a four-game losing streak has darkened the Oilers’ door. The Oilers are bushed, coming off a six-game Eastern swing with two back-to-backs, and a disciplined Vegas team smartly took advantage of the Oilers’ state. “I didn’t think we were very good with the puck,” began Connor McDavid, who was by his standards below average on Tuesday. “It’s been a tough stretch, obviously. A lot of games, a lot of travel, a lot of late nights. There’s no excuse.” The Oilers beat the Florida Panthers exactly a week before in Sunrise, outplaying a Panthers team that was on the final game of a stretch of seven games in 11 days. “The brains were right. The hands and the legs weren’t there,” Florida head coach Paul Maurice said of his team that night. “The will was there, the heart was there … We just couldn’t get to some of the places we needed to get to.” In hockey, where players are young, fit, and fly on luxurious charters with hotel-to-hotel service, the word “tired” is not defined by sore muscles and aching backs. Tired means shlepping from town to town, from time zone to time zone, with barely any time in between to unpack. And its results show up in mental lapses like Tuesday’s, where some familiar maladies arose in a season where many of these Oilers have kicked those old habits. Remember Leon Draisaitl and that turnover at the offensive blueline? He’d mostly eliminated that from his game, until this last four-game stretch.

Could this year be an outlier? There are multiple checkpoints throughout each NHL season where teams assess their competitive hopes, and U.S. Thanksgiving is traditionally a very important one. Every team has just recently passed the first quarter of the regular season, and there's still a ton of hockey to be played. Over the past five seasons, 11 of the 16 teams who qualify for the Stanley Cup playoffs were in post-season positions at American Thanksgiving. According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman, the Panthers have placed Cole Schwindt on waivers. As much as it would hurt to lose two forwards in a matter of days, Florida is […]
items.body: Register Login Panthers Place Cole Schwindt On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at November 24, 2026 2:37 pm A day after losing forward Cole Reinhardt on waivers to the Vancouver Canucks, the Florida Panthers are exposing another forward to the other 31 teams. According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , the Panthers have placed Cole Schwindt on waivers. As much as it would hurt to lose two forwards in a matter of days, Florida is expected to return Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand for tomorrow’s contest against the Ottawa Senators. With respect to Reinhardt and Schwindt, the Panthers would comfortably make that swap 11 out of 10 times. Like Reinhardt, Schwindt made his way to Florida via waivers. The Panthers claimed the bottom-six forward a few days before the puck dropped in the 2025-26 season. He spent the entire regular season with Florida, scoring five goals and seven points in 29 games with a +2 rating. He also displayed decent physicality by blocking 11 shots and delivering 39 hits. This year, aside from a five-game stretch with the Charlotte Checkers in the AHL, Schwindt has again featured with the Panthers. Unfortunately, he hasn’t been productive, going scoreless in 15 appearances with a -5 rating, while averaging 8:28 of ice time per game. Still, he looked good with the Checkers, registering one goal and three points. If he clears waivers, unlike Reinhardt, the Panthers will likely assign Schwindt back to Charlotte. Still, he’s signed through next season at a league minimum salary, and a forward-needy team might be interested in him.

items.title: Islanders place Kyle Palmieri on injured reserve
items.summary: Palmieri left Monday’s 4-2 loss to the Leafs with a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The New York Islanders have finally provided a status for Kyle Palmieri, as the winger was placed on injured reserve earlier on Tuesday. This transaction comes in the wake of Monday’s 4-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs , where Palmieri sustained a lower-body injury in the second period after an awkward fall caused him to fall into the Islanders net. He left the game shortly after, and was announced as out for the rest of the game ahead of the third period. Palmieri’s status was unknown to start Tuesday, as even when the Islanders held a practice, no update was provided on him other than that he was seeing the doctor that day to get a proper prognosis. While the Islanders have yet to make a formal announcement of Palmieri’s timeline for return, an IR placement at least confirms that he will miss at least the next seven days with his injury, as he is not allowed to be activated off of IR within that time. The Islanders play three games within the next seven days. At this point in time, no other roster moves have been made in response to Palmieri’s IR placement. Palmieri has had a slow start to the season by his standards, as he has just four goals and five assists for nine points in 23 games . It’s the worst scoring pace of his career since establishing himself as an NHL regular in 2013, although it should be expected for a player who is now 35 years old. With Palmieri out of the lineup, Mathew Barzal is expected to replace the Smithtown, New York product on the top line alongside Bo Horvat and Simon Holmstrom. In the last three seasons, this trio has held the score even at 3-3 and has a 36.18% 5v5 expected goal share in 58:49 of ice time, according to Natural Stat Trick . Mitchell Chaffee is expected to draw into the lineup in place of Palmieri.

items.title: Can Michael Hage Become For The Red Wings What Jarome Iginla Was For The Flames?
items.summary: Michael Hage has the potential to be the kind of player who will make the Detroit Red Wings forget about Dylan Larkin.
items.body: Nov 24, 2026 8:15 PM Published Nov 24, 2026 8:15 PM Michael Hage has the potential to be the kind of player who will make the Detroit Red Wings forget about Dylan Larkin. Montreal Canadiens GM Kent Hughes knows he's giving up a great young player and NHL prospect in Michael Hage in the Dylan Larkin trade. But this is precisely why the previously bottom-feeder Canadiens have been stockpiling prospects over the years. Either Hage was going to come in and be a very good player for them or the Canadiens were going to use him to acquire a piece they need now . Hage, who was the ninth best NHL-affiliated propsect in this year's THN Future Watch edition, has the potential to be that kind of player. Someone who will make the Detroit Red Wings forget about Dylan Larkin. The trade that comes to mind for me is in 1995 when the Dallas Stars did just what the Canadiens are doing now. They dealt away a top prospect named Jarome Iginla to get Joe Nieuwendyk in a blockbuster deal. Nieuwendyk went on to help deliver the Stars their only Stanley Cup, while Iginla went on to forge a Hall of Fame career with the Calgary Flames .

items.title: Travis Green a major factor in Senators overcoming Brady Tkachuk trade
items.summary: Steve Peters joined Daily Faceoff Live to talk about the Senators and how Green has helped their success this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn A lot of people counted out the Ottawa Senators after Brady Tkachuk’s trade request forced a move to the Florida Panthers , especially when it felt like the Sens didn’t get a player of a similar calibre to their former captain. And yet, almost two months into the season and the Senators sit atop the Atlantic Division with a 16-6-3 record , and could be the class of the toughest division in the league. A lot of that success should be credited to head coach Travis Green, who is getting Ottawa to play to the sum of their parts to compensate for the talent they lost in Tkachuk. Steve Peters joined Daily Faceoff Live to talk about the Senators and how Green has helped their success this season. Steve Peters: When I make mistakes or say something foolish, I’m going to come back and tell you. I thought this was going to be a difficult start for the Ottawa Senators losing Brady Tkachuk. I know what that might have done to the room. But it did the opposite. Guys said, “Okay, we don’t have him. Let’s do it together.” This is one of those [teams] where the sum of their parts are better than their individual pieces. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If the Washington Capitals and Dallas Stars are playing a game of waiver tennis, then the ball is back in Washington’s court. On Tuesday, the Capitals claimed goaltender Remi Poirier off waivers from the Stars. Poirier, 25, has been on quite the hectic journey in the early going of this season. After spending the preseason with the Stars, he was placed on waivers by Dallas just before the regular season and claimed by the New Jersey Devils . On November 1, the Devils traded him to the Capitals in exchange for a 2027 seventh-round pick. Just a week later, on November 8, he was placed on waivers again, and this time claimed back by the Stars. On Monday, Dallas placed him on waivers yet again. With all of his scrambling about, he has yet to get into an NHL game this season. He has appeared in three games for the Texas Stars of the American Hockey League (AHL), where he posted a 2-1-0 record with a .938 save percentage and a 2.02 goals-against average. The Farnham, Quebec native played all of last season Texas as well, putting up a 27-19-6 record to go along with a .912 SV% and a 2.61 GAA in 52 appearances. Selected by Dallas in the sixth round of the 2020 NHL Entry Draft, Poirier has yet to make an NHL appearance in his career. After his four-year junior career with the Gatineau Olympiques of the Quebec Maritimes Junior Hockey League (QMJHL), he joined the Stars organization in the 2022-23 season, splitting between the ECHL’s Idaho Steelheads and Texas. He spent the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons entirely with Texas, compiling a 34-27-6 record with a .906 SV% and a 2.85 GAA. items.title: Canadiens will only benefit from full Larkin effect once Demidov returns
items.summary: It feels like it’ll be at least one more week before we see the full Dylan Larkin effect with the Montreal Canadiens, because it appears as though it’ll take at least that long before we see Ivan Demidov beside him.
items.body: BROSSARD, Que. — It feels like it’ll be at least one more week before we see the full Dylan Larkin effect with the Montreal Canadiens , because it appears as though it’ll take at least that long before we see Ivan Demidov beside him. This was one of the motivating factors in sacrificing top prospect Michael Hage in the package for Larkin, to get Demidov a top centre to play with right away. But Demidov hasn’t been able to play since Game 2 of the season. The fracture he sustained in his right foot during pre-season has been healing much slower than expected — the initial timeline for his recovery, advanced by the Canadiens on Oct. 6, was supposed to be two to four weeks — and it doesn’t appear he’ll be at 100 per cent before the team is prepared to play the final game of its upcoming road trip through Denver, Las Vegas and Utah. On Monday, Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes told Sportsnet it would just be a matter of days before the Russian winger could return to action, though he couldn’t say how many. Then, on Tuesday, the Canadiens recalled winger Brett Berard to take Demidov’s place on the roster. Unless something changes between now and next Monday, his place next to Larkin will be filled by another teammate. Alex Newhook and Alex Texier flanked Larkin in his first game with the team — a 2-1 loss to the Los Angeles Kings — and fared reasonably well. They combined on the play that netted the Canadiens their only goal and controlled 60 per cent of the shot attempts and 83 per cent of the expected goals at five-on-five. items.body: Register Login Wild Place Calvin Pickard On Waivers By Gabriel Foley | at November 24, 2026 1:27 pm Following Filip Gustavsson ’s season debut on Monday, the Minnesota Wild have placed third-string goaltender Calvin Pickard on waivers. This will solidify Minnesota’s goaltending duo after Gustavsson recovered from his offseason hip surgery. Pickard appeared in three games while serving as backup to Jesper Wallstedt through the start of the season. He set a 1-1-1 record with a .855 save percentage and 3.60 goals-against-average. Minnesota signed Pickard to a one-year, $1MM contract over the summer. That deal will maintain his $1MM salary through an assignment to the minor-leagues – a small perk for the veteran of 15 pro seasons. Across his career, Pickard has recorded a 161-117-40 record and .913 save percentage in 329 AHL games. He has also set a 75-78-15 record and .900 save percentage in 194 NHL games. Now 34 years old, he brings the leadership of a seasoned pro to Minnesota’s depth chart. A seven-figure salary will likely prevent any teams from claiming Pickard, setting him up for a second-straight season of AHL minutes. Pickard could take over an Iowa Wild crease that has been split between Riley Mercer and William Rousseau . The two have nearly identical stat lines – with Mercer setting a 3-5-2 record and .900 save percentage in 10 games while Rousseau has a 3-5-1 record and .899 save percentage in nine games. Notably, Rousseau is on an AHL contract, which could make him the most expendable option in a room with two other goalies on NHL deals. Rousseau could even be a candidate for a move to the ECHL, though it’ll be to a new team after the Iowa Heartlanders folded over the summer. Minnesota is now affiliated with the Jacksonville Icemen.

items.title: Islanders’ Ryan Pulock out 1-2 weeks with upper-body injury
items.summary: Pulock has not appeared for the Islanders since November 19.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images The New York Islanders got clarity on the length of time they will have to go without a key veteran defenseman, as the team announced on Tuesday that Ryan Pulock will be out for one to two weeks with his upper-body injury. Pulock has not played since he suffered the injury in a 4-3 overtime loss to the Winnipeg Jets on November 19, meaning the Isles have been without the steady right-hander for their past two games, a win over the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday as well as their 4-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday. A 32-year-old Manitoba native, Pulock is in the midst of his 12th NHL season, all of which have come as a member of the Islanders. The right-hander has appeared in 17 games this season, notching four assists and posting a plus-7 rating on an average of 17:35 of time on ice per game. That role reflects the least amount of ice time Pulock has garnered in any full season in the league. Pulock is in the fifth season of an eight-year contract that carries a salary cap hit of $6.15 million. The Islanders, playing in their first full season under head coach Peter DeBoer, have mostly held on to a playoff spot throughout the first two months of the year, but the loss to the Leafs on Monday caused them to fall out of the picture by both total points and points percentage. New York is effectively tied for the third-place spot in the Metropolitan Division with their rival New York Rangers , but trails the Florida Panthers for the second wild card spot for the time being.
